example_sentences.de: Das Restaurant ist heute geschlossen.
example_sentences.en: The restaurant is closed today.

example_sentences.de: Kennst du ein gutes Restaurant hier in der Nähe?
example_sentences.en: Do you know a good restaurant near here?

cloze.de: Wir gehen heute Abend in ein italienisches ___.
cloze.en: We're going to an Italian restaurant tonight.

words.notes: Pronounced in the French way: 'Restorãː'. The final -t is soft.
words.mnemonic: Same word as English, so it takes the 'foreign' neuter: das Restaurant.
words.germany_context: In many German restaurants you seat yourself — just look for a free table and sit down. Only in fancier places or when a sign says 'Sie werden platziert' do you wait to be seated.

example_sentences.de: Das Café an der Ecke hat sehr guten Kuchen.
example_sentences.en: The café on the corner has very good cake.

example_sentences.de: Treffen wir uns um drei im Café?
example_sentences.en: Shall we meet at the café at three?

cloze.de: Ich arbeite oft in einem ___ mit WLAN.
cloze.en: I often work in a café with Wi-Fi.

words.notes: Note the accent: Café (the place) vs. Kaffee (the drink).
words.mnemonic: Café with an é is the place; Kaffee with two e's is the drink.
words.germany_context: Sunday afternoon 'Kaffee und Kuchen' around 15:00 is a real institution — cafés are packed, so reserve for larger groups.

example_sentences.de: In der Kneipe war es gestern sehr laut.
example_sentences.en: It was very loud in the pub yesterday.

example_sentences.de: Wir trinken noch ein Bier in der Kneipe.
example_sentences.en: We're having another beer at the pub.

cloze.de: Nach der Arbeit gehen die Kollegen in die ___.
cloze.en: After work the colleagues go to the pub.

words.notes: A Kneipe is a simple, cosy neighbourhood pub — food is basic, beer is the point.
words.mnemonic: Kneipe sounds like 'knee-pa' — where you rest your knees after work.
words.germany_context: Kneipen are usually cash-friendly and often cash-only; you pay at your table when you leave, not at the bar.

example_sentences.de: Die Bar macht erst um acht Uhr auf.
example_sentences.en: The bar doesn't open until eight o'clock.

example_sentences.de: An der Bar gibt es gute Cocktails.
example_sentences.en: There are good cocktails at the bar.

cloze.de: Wir haben uns in einer kleinen ___ in Kreuzberg getroffen.
cloze.en: We met in a small bar in Kreuzberg.

words.notes: 'An der Bar' can mean both 'at the bar counter' and 'at the bar venue'.
words.mnemonic: Die Bar — foreign but feminine, like die Party.

example_sentences.de: Am Bahnhof gibt es einen türkischen Imbiss.
example_sentences.en: There is a Turkish snack bar at the station.

example_sentences.de: Der Imbiss hat bis Mitternacht offen.
example_sentences.en: The snack bar is open until midnight.

cloze.de: Mittags esse ich schnell etwas am ___.
cloze.en: At lunchtime I quickly eat something at the snack bar.

words.notes: Imbiss = the small stand or shop; 'Dönerbude' and 'Pommesbude' are informal versions.
words.mnemonic: Imbiss ~ 'in-bite' — a quick bite standing up.
words.germany_context: Imbisse are almost always cash-only and are one of the few places open late and on Sundays, when supermarkets are shut.

example_sentences.de: Die Öffnungszeiten stehen an der Tür.
example_sentences.en: The opening hours are on the door.

example_sentences.de: Hat das Café am Sonntag andere Öffnungszeiten?
example_sentences.en: Does the café have different opening hours on Sunday?

cloze.de: Bitte beachten Sie unsere neue ___ ab Montag.
cloze.en: Please note our new opening time from Monday.

words.notes: Almost always used in the plural: die Öffnungszeiten.
words.mnemonic: öffnen + Zeit: the time when it opens.
words.germany_context: Shops are closed on Sundays and public holidays by law; restaurants and cafés may open, but many have a Ruhetag and a break between lunch and dinner.

example_sentences.de: In der Metzgerei kaufe ich frische Wurst.
example_sentences.en: I buy fresh sausage at the butcher's shop.

example_sentences.de: Die Metzgerei um die Ecke ist sehr gut.
example_sentences.en: The butcher's shop around the corner is very good.

cloze.de: Mittags gibt es in der ___ auch warme Gerichte.
cloze.en: At lunchtime the butcher's shop also serves warm dishes.

words.notes: In northern Germany people often say 'Fleischerei' or 'Schlachterei' instead.
words.mnemonic: -ei → die, like die Bäckerei.
words.germany_context: Many Metzgereien have a small lunch counter with cheap hot meals — a local secret for a quick, good-value Mittagessen.

example_sentences.de: Im Sommer sitzen wir gern im Biergarten.
example_sentences.en: In summer we like sitting in the beer garden.

example_sentences.de: Der Biergarten ist bei gutem Wetter voll.
example_sentences.en: The beer garden is full when the weather is good.

cloze.de: Am Sonntag treffen wir uns im ___ am See.
cloze.en: On Sunday we're meeting at the beer garden by the lake.

words.notes: Der Garten → der Biergarten. The last part of a compound decides the gender.
words.mnemonic: der Garten stays der in every compound.
words.germany_context: In a traditional Biergarten you may bring your own food but must buy the drinks there; you order and pay at the counter, so no tip is expected.

example_sentences.de: Der Kellner bringt gleich die Getränke.
example_sentences.en: The waiter is bringing the drinks right away.

example_sentences.de: Wir haben den Kellner nach der Rechnung gefragt.
example_sentences.en: We asked the waiter for the bill.

cloze.de: Entschuldigung, wo ist der ___?
cloze.en: Excuse me, where is the waiter?

words.notes: Never call a waiter with 'Herr Ober!' — that is very old-fashioned. Just say 'Entschuldigung'.
words.mnemonic: Kellner ~ 'cellar-man' bringing up the wine.
words.germany_context: Waiters do not check on you constantly; making eye contact or raising a hand is the normal, polite way to get attention.

example_sentences.de: Die Kellnerin war heute sehr freundlich.
example_sentences.en: The waitress was very friendly today.

example_sentences.de: Frag bitte die Kellnerin nach der Speisekarte.
example_sentences.en: Please ask the waitress for the menu.

cloze.de: Die ___ hat unsere Bestellung aufgeschrieben.
cloze.en: The waitress wrote down our order.

words.notes: -in makes the female form and is always feminine: der Kellner → die Kellnerin.
words.mnemonic: -in → die, always.

example_sentences.de: Die Bedienung war leider sehr langsam.
example_sentences.en: The service was unfortunately very slow.

example_sentences.de: Ich rufe kurz die Bedienung.
example_sentences.en: I'll call the server for a moment.

cloze.de: Das Essen war gut und die ___ auch.
cloze.en: The food was good and so was the service.

words.notes: Bedienung means both the service and the person serving you — a neutral word for waiter or waitress.
words.mnemonic: -ung → die, always.
words.germany_context: 'Selbstbedienung' (self-service) on a sign means you order and collect at the counter — and no tip is expected there.

example_sentences.de: Können wir bitte die Speisekarte haben?
example_sentences.en: Could we have the menu, please?

example_sentences.de: Auf der Speisekarte steht alles auf Deutsch.
example_sentences.en: Everything on the menu is in German.

cloze.de: Der Kellner bringt uns gleich die ___.
cloze.en: The waiter will bring us the menu shortly.

words.notes: Often shortened to just 'die Karte': 'Die Karte, bitte.'
words.mnemonic: die Karte → die Speisekarte; all -karte compounds are feminine.
words.germany_context: Many places only have a German menu; an English one usually exists only in tourist areas — ask 'Haben Sie eine Karte auf Englisch?'

example_sentences.de: Die Tageskarte hängt an der Tür.
example_sentences.en: The daily menu is hanging on the door.

example_sentences.de: Auf der Tageskarte steht heute Fisch.
example_sentences.en: Today there is fish on the daily menu.

cloze.de: Haben Sie auch eine ___?
cloze.en: Do you also have a menu of the day?

words.notes: Careful: 'Tageskarte' also means a day ticket for public transport.
words.mnemonic: Karte of the Tag — the dishes only for today.
words.germany_context: The 'Mittagstisch' or Tageskarte at lunchtime is usually much cheaper than the evening menu — a common way to eat well for under 12 euros.

example_sentences.de: Könnte ich bitte die Getränkekarte sehen?
example_sentences.en: Could I see the drinks menu, please?

example_sentences.de: Die Getränkekarte liegt auf dem Tisch.
example_sentences.en: The drinks menu is on the table.

cloze.de: Auf der ___ stehen viele Weine aus der Region.
cloze.en: There are many regional wines on the drinks menu.

words.notes: Often the drinks are printed on the back of the Speisekarte.
words.mnemonic: Getränke + Karte → the card of drinks.

example_sentences.de: Dieses Gericht ist sehr beliebt.
example_sentences.en: This dish is very popular.

example_sentences.de: Gibt es auch Gerichte ohne Fleisch?
example_sentences.en: Are there also dishes without meat?

cloze.de: Welches ___ können Sie mir empfehlen?
cloze.en: Which dish can you recommend to me?

words.notes: False friend alert: 'das Gericht' also means 'court of law'. Context makes it clear.
words.mnemonic: Ge- words are usually neuter: das Gericht, das Getränk, das Geschäft.

example_sentences.de: Das Menü kostet 15 Euro.
example_sentences.en: The set meal costs 15 euros.

example_sentences.de: Wir nehmen zweimal das Menü.
example_sentences.en: We'll take the set meal twice.

cloze.de: Im ___ sind Suppe und Nachtisch inklusive.
cloze.en: Soup and dessert are included in the set meal.

words.notes: False friend: 'Menü' is a fixed multi-course meal, not the list of dishes. The list is 'die Speisekarte'.
words.mnemonic: Menü = several courses; Karte = the list.

example_sentences.de: Ich möchte meine Bestellung ändern.
example_sentences.en: I would like to change my order.

example_sentences.de: Die Bestellung dauert heute leider länger.
example_sentences.en: The order is unfortunately taking longer today.

cloze.de: Darf ich Ihre ___ aufnehmen?
cloze.en: May I take your order?

words.notes: 'Die Bestellung aufnehmen' is the fixed phrase waiters use for taking an order.
words.mnemonic: -ung → die, always.

example_sentences.de: Als Beilage nehme ich Salat.
example_sentences.en: I'll have salad as a side dish.

example_sentences.de: Welche Beilagen gibt es?
example_sentences.en: What side dishes are there?

cloze.de: Zum Schnitzel bekommen Sie eine ___ Ihrer Wahl.
cloze.en: With the schnitzel you get a side dish of your choice.

words.notes: Typical Beilagen: Pommes, Kartoffeln, Reis, Salat, Gemüse.
words.mnemonic: bei + legen = laid beside the main dish.

example_sentences.de: In der Kantine essen wir jeden Mittag.
example_sentences.en: We eat in the canteen every lunchtime.

example_sentences.de: Die Kantine hat nur bis zwei Uhr offen.
example_sentences.en: The canteen is only open until two o'clock.

cloze.de: Unsere Firma hat eine eigene ___.
cloze.en: Our company has its own canteen.

words.notes: Company canteen = die Kantine; university canteen = die Mensa.
words.mnemonic: -ine → die, like die Maschine.
words.germany_context: Most larger German companies have a subsidised Kantine where lunch costs a few euros and colleagues eat together at fixed times, usually before 13:00.

example_sentences.de: Wir bestellen heute beim Lieferdienst.
example_sentences.en: We're ordering from the delivery service today.

example_sentences.de: Der Lieferdienst braucht ungefähr 40 Minuten.
example_sentences.en: The delivery service takes about 40 minutes.

cloze.de: Kennst du einen guten ___ für Pizza?
cloze.en: Do you know a good delivery service for pizza?

words.notes: der Dienst → der Lieferdienst. The verb is 'liefern' (to deliver).
words.mnemonic: liefern + Dienst: the delivery service.
words.germany_context: Delivery drivers expect a small tip in cash, one or two euros, even when you pay for the food by app.

example_sentences.de: Das Buffet ist von sieben bis zehn Uhr geöffnet.
example_sentences.en: The buffet is open from seven to ten o'clock.

example_sentences.de: Am Buffet kann man so viel nehmen, wie man möchte.
example_sentences.en: At the buffet you can take as much as you like.

cloze.de: Im Hotel gibt es ein großes ___ zum Frühstück.
cloze.en: At the hotel there's a big buffet for breakfast.

words.notes: Pronounced 'bü-FEE'. Often written 'Büfett' in older texts.
words.mnemonic: French word, so neuter like das Restaurant.
words.germany_context: Sunday brunch buffets in cafés are popular and usually cost a fixed price per person; drinks are almost always extra.

example_sentences.de: Was ist die Spezialität des Hauses?
example_sentences.en: What is the speciality of the house?

example_sentences.de: Weißwurst ist eine bayerische Spezialität.
example_sentences.en: Weisswurst is a Bavarian speciality.

cloze.de: Diese ___ gibt es nur hier in der Region.
cloze.en: You can only get this speciality here in the region.

words.notes: Nouns ending in -tät are always feminine: die Spezialität, die Universität, die Qualität.
words.mnemonic: -tät → die, always.
words.germany_context: German food is strongly regional: Weißwurst in Bavaria, Currywurst in Berlin, Labskaus in Hamburg — asking for the local Spezialität always works.

example_sentences.de: Ich habe eine Reservierung auf den Namen Yalcin.
example_sentences.en: I have a reservation under the name Yalcin.

example_sentences.de: Brauchen wir am Samstag eine Reservierung?
example_sentences.en: Do we need a reservation on Saturday?

cloze.de: Ohne ___ bekommen wir am Wochenende keinen Tisch.
cloze.en: Without a reservation we won't get a table at the weekend.

words.notes: The verb is 'reservieren': 'Ich möchte einen Tisch reservieren.'
words.mnemonic: -ung → die, always.
words.germany_context: Reserved tables carry a small 'Reserviert' sign — never sit at one, even if the restaurant looks empty.

example_sentences.de: Die Rechnung stimmt nicht.
example_sentences.en: The bill isn't correct.

example_sentences.de: Können wir bitte die Rechnung haben?
example_sentences.en: Could we have the bill, please?

cloze.de: Auf der ___ stehen drei Bier und zwei Schnitzel.
cloze.en: There are three beers and two schnitzels on the bill.

words.notes: 'Die Rechnung, bitte' is the standard way to ask for the bill.
words.mnemonic: -ung → die. From rechnen (to calculate).
words.germany_context: You pay at the table, not at a till: the server comes over with a card reader or a wallet, and everyone pays right there.

example_sentences.de: Wir geben immer ein bisschen Trinkgeld.
example_sentences.en: We always leave a little tip.

example_sentences.de: Ist das Trinkgeld schon in der Rechnung?
example_sentences.en: Is the tip already included in the bill?

cloze.de: Zehn Prozent ___ sind hier völlig normal.
cloze.en: A ten percent tip is completely normal here.

words.notes: das Geld → das Trinkgeld. Literally 'drink money'.
words.mnemonic: Money for the waiter's drink.
words.germany_context: Tip about 5-10% by rounding up. Don't leave coins on the table: say the total you want to pay out loud when handing over the money, e.g. 'Machen Sie 25' for a 23,40 bill.

example_sentences.de: Kann ich bitte eine Quittung bekommen?
example_sentences.en: Could I get a receipt, please?

example_sentences.de: Ich brauche die Quittung für die Firma.
example_sentences.en: I need the receipt for the company.

cloze.de: Ohne ___ bekomme ich das Geld nicht zurück.
cloze.en: Without a receipt I won't get the money back.

words.notes: 'Der Kassenbon' or 'der Beleg' are used in shops; 'die Quittung' works everywhere.
words.mnemonic: -ung → die, always.
words.germany_context: If you want to claim a meal as a business expense, ask for a 'Bewirtungsbeleg' — a receipt with the restaurant's tax details.

example_sentences.de: Ich habe leider kein Bargeld dabei.
example_sentences.en: Unfortunately I don't have any cash on me.

example_sentences.de: Hier kann man nur mit Bargeld zahlen.
example_sentences.en: Here you can only pay with cash.

cloze.de: Nimm lieber etwas ___ mit, das Café hat keine Kartenzahlung.
cloze.en: Better take some cash with you, the café doesn't take cards.

words.notes: 'Bar zahlen' = to pay cash. 'Nur Barzahlung' on a sign means cash only.
words.mnemonic: das Geld → das Bargeld.
words.germany_context: Germany still loves cash: plenty of restaurants, Imbisse and Kneipen are cash-only, and many take only Girocard, not Visa or Mastercard. Always carry 20-30 euros.

example_sentences.de: Bitte zahlen Sie vorne an der Kasse.
example_sentences.en: Please pay at the till at the front.

example_sentences.de: An der Kasse steht eine lange Schlange.
example_sentences.en: There is a long queue at the till.

cloze.de: Im Café bestellt man direkt an der ___.
cloze.en: In the café you order directly at the till.

words.notes: In a sit-down restaurant you do NOT go to the Kasse — the server settles up at your table.
words.mnemonic: Kasse ~ 'cash' desk.
words.germany_context: Self-service cafés and bakeries take payment at the Kasse; in a proper restaurant, waiting at the till looks odd — stay seated and say 'Zahlen, bitte'.

example_sentences.de: Kann ich mit EC-Karte zahlen?
example_sentences.en: Can I pay by debit card?

example_sentences.de: Meine EC-Karte funktioniert heute nicht.
example_sentences.en: My debit card isn't working today.

cloze.de: Wir nehmen nur ___, keine Kreditkarte.
cloze.en: We only take debit cards, no credit cards.

words.notes: die Karte → die EC-Karte. Officially called 'Girocard' now, but everyone says EC-Karte.
words.mnemonic: die Karte stays die in every compound.
words.germany_context: 'Wir nehmen nur EC' is extremely common — German debit cards work almost everywhere, foreign credit cards often don't.

example_sentences.de: Montag ist Ruhetag.
example_sentences.en: Monday is our closing day.

example_sentences.de: Das Lokal hat zwei Ruhetage pro Woche.
example_sentences.en: The restaurant has two closing days per week.

cloze.de: Wir waren umsonst da, dienstags ist ___.
cloze.en: We went there for nothing, Tuesday is the closing day.

words.notes: der Tag → der Ruhetag. You'll see it on the door: 'Ruhetag: Montag'.
words.mnemonic: Ruhe = rest, Tag = day: the day the kitchen rests.
words.germany_context: Most family-run restaurants close one fixed day a week, and many kitchens also stop serving hot food between about 14:00 and 17:30 — always check before turning up.

example_sentences.de: Ist dieser Platz noch frei?
example_sentences.en: Is this seat still free?

example_sentences.de: Draußen gibt es keine Plätze mehr.
example_sentences.en: There are no seats left outside.

cloze.de: Nehmen Sie bitte ___!
cloze.en: Please have a seat!

words.notes: 'Platz nehmen' = to take a seat. 'Der Platz' also means a public square.
words.mnemonic: Platz ~ 'place'.
words.germany_context: When a café is full, Germans often share a table: ask 'Ist hier noch frei?' and sitting down with strangers is completely normal.

example_sentences.de: Er ist hier Stammgast und kennt alle Kellner.
example_sentences.en: He's a regular here and knows all the waiters.

example_sentences.de: Stammgäste bekommen manchmal einen Schnaps aufs Haus.
example_sentences.en: Regulars sometimes get a schnapps on the house.

cloze.de: Nach zwei Jahren bin ich in diesem Café ___.
cloze.en: After two years I'm a regular at this café.

words.notes: der Gast → der Stammgast. Plural with umlaut: die Stammgäste.
words.mnemonic: Stamm = core, Gast = guest: one of the core guests.
words.germany_context: Becoming a Stammgast in your local Kneipe is one of the easiest ways to get to know neighbours — staff will start greeting you by name.

example_sentences.de: Diese Runde geht auf mich.
example_sentences.en: This round is on me.

example_sentences.de: Er hat eine Runde für alle bestellt.
example_sentences.en: He ordered a round for everyone.

cloze.de: Wer zahlt die nächste ___?
cloze.en: Who is paying for the next round?

words.notes: 'Eine Runde ausgeben' = to buy a round for everybody.
words.mnemonic: A round goes round the table.
words.germany_context: Buying a Runde is common among friends and colleagues, and people keep loose track of whose turn it is next time.

example_sentences.de: Einmal Pommes mit Mayo, bitte.
example_sentences.en: One portion of fries with mayo, please.

example_sentences.de: Die Pommes sind leider kalt.
example_sentences.en: Unfortunately the fries are cold.

cloze.de: Möchten Sie ___ oder Salat dazu?
cloze.en: Would you like fries or salad with that?

words.notes: Plural only, always 'die Pommes'. Pronounced 'POM-mes' in Germany.
words.mnemonic: Plural-only, like die Eltern and die Leute.
words.germany_context: At an Imbiss you'll be asked 'Rot oder weiß?' — ketchup or mayo. 'Pommes Schranke' means both.

example_sentences.de: Eine Currywurst mit Pommes, bitte.
example_sentences.en: One currywurst with fries, please.

example_sentences.de: Die Currywurst kostet nur vier Euro.
example_sentences.en: The currywurst costs only four euros.

cloze.de: In Berlin muss man einmal ___ probieren.
cloze.en: In Berlin you have to try currywurst once.

words.notes: die Wurst → die Currywurst.
words.mnemonic: die Wurst stays die in every compound.
words.germany_context: The classic cheap German street food, especially in Berlin and the Ruhr area; Imbiss stands sell it into the night and usually take cash only.

example_sentences.de: Am Sonntag gehen wir zum Brunch.
example_sentences.en: On Sunday we're going for brunch.

example_sentences.de: Der Brunch kostet 22 Euro pro Person.
example_sentences.en: The brunch costs 22 euros per person.

cloze.de: Für den ___ am Sonntag brauchen wir eine Reservierung.
cloze.en: For brunch on Sunday we need a reservation.

words.notes: Pronounced like in English. Masculine, like der Lunch.
words.mnemonic: breakfast + lunch = der Brunch.
words.germany_context: Sunday brunch is a small institution in German cities and one of the few things open on a Sunday — popular cafés are booked out days in advance.

example_sentences.de: Ich möchte bitte zahlen.
example_sentences.en: I'd like to pay, please.

example_sentences.de: Zahlst du mit Karte oder bar?
example_sentences.en: Are you paying by card or cash?

cloze.de: Wir ___ heute getrennt.
cloze.en: We're paying separately today.

words.notes: 'Zahlen' is short and standard in restaurants; 'bezahlen' is used more with an object: 'die Rechnung bezahlen'.
words.mnemonic: zahlen ~ 'to pay' the Zahl (number).
words.germany_context: Catch the server's eye and say 'Zahlen, bitte' — you settle up at your table, and each person tells the server their own total if you're splitting.

example_sentences.de: Was empfehlen Sie uns?
example_sentences.en: What do you recommend to us?

example_sentences.de: Er empfiehlt immer den Fisch.
example_sentences.en: He always recommends the fish.

cloze.de: Können Sie mir eine Spezialität ___?
cloze.en: Can you recommend a speciality to me?

words.notes: Strong verb with e→ie in du/er: du empfiehlst, er empfiehlt. Person in dative, thing in accusative.
words.mnemonic: Like nehmen and geben, the stem vowel shifts in du/er forms.
words.germany_context: Asking 'Was können Sie empfehlen?' is normal and welcome — servers will happily point you to the Tageskarte.

example_sentences.de: Werden Sie schon bedient?
example_sentences.en: Are you being served yet?

example_sentences.de: Heute bedient nur eine Kellnerin.
example_sentences.en: Only one waitress is serving today.

cloze.de: Draußen ___ wir leider nicht.
cloze.en: Unfortunately we don't serve outside.

words.notes: 'Werden Sie schon bedient?' is what a server asks to check if someone already took your order.
words.mnemonic: die Bedienung comes from bedienen.
words.germany_context: In a Biergarten or self-service café nobody comes to your table at all — the sign says 'Selbstbedienung' and you order at the counter.

example_sentences.de: Der Kellner räumt die Teller ab.
example_sentences.en: The waiter clears away the plates.

example_sentences.de: Darf ich schon abräumen?
example_sentences.en: May I clear the table already?

cloze.de: Bitte ___ Sie die Gläser noch nicht ab.
cloze.en: Please don't clear the glasses away yet.

words.notes: Separable: the 'ab' goes to the end of the sentence.
words.mnemonic: ab = away, räumen = to clear: clear away.
words.germany_context: 'Darf ich schon abräumen?' often comes right after you put your cutlery together on the plate — that's the signal that you've finished.

example_sentences.de: Haben Sie auch vegane Gerichte?
example_sentences.en: Do you also have vegan dishes?

example_sentences.de: Meine Freundin lebt seit zwei Jahren vegan.
example_sentences.en: My girlfriend has been living vegan for two years.

cloze.de: Ist dieser Kuchen ___?
cloze.en: Is this cake vegan?

words.notes: Pronounced 've-GAAN' with a long a.
words.mnemonic: Same word as in English, just a German stress on the second syllable.
words.germany_context: Germany is very vegan-friendly: menus mark dishes with a small 'v' or 'vegan', and every supermarket has a vegan section.

example_sentences.de: Ist die Suppe glutenfrei?
example_sentences.en: Is the soup gluten-free?

example_sentences.de: Wir haben auch glutenfreies Brot.
example_sentences.en: We also have gluten-free bread.

cloze.de: Können Sie mir sagen, ob die Soße ___ ist?
cloze.en: Can you tell me whether the sauce is gluten-free?

words.notes: The suffix -frei means 'free of': alkoholfrei, koffeinfrei, laktosefrei.
words.mnemonic: -frei = free of, exactly like the English '-free'.
words.germany_context: Allergens are listed by number in the small print of German menus — a footnote key at the bottom of the page explains what each number means.

example_sentences.de: Haben Sie laktosefreie Milch für den Kaffee?
example_sentences.en: Do you have lactose-free milk for the coffee?

example_sentences.de: Dieser Käse ist laktosefrei.
example_sentences.en: This cheese is lactose-free.

cloze.de: Diese Sahne ist ___, du kannst sie essen.
cloze.en: This cream is lactose-free, you can eat it.

words.notes: Note the German spelling with k: Laktose, not 'lactose'.
words.mnemonic: Laktose + frei = free of lactose.
words.germany_context: Supermarkets and larger cafés almost always stock laktosefreie Milch and Hafermilch (oat milk) — just ask for a 'Hafermilch-Latte'.

example_sentences.de: Alle Kuchen sind hausgemacht.
example_sentences.en: All the cakes are home-made.

example_sentences.de: Die hausgemachte Limonade schmeckt super.
example_sentences.en: The home-made lemonade tastes great.

cloze.de: Ist die Soße ___ oder aus der Tüte?
cloze.en: Is the sauce home-made or out of a packet?

words.notes: 'Hausgemacht' and 'selbst gemacht' mean the same on a menu.
words.mnemonic: Haus + gemacht = made in the house.

example_sentences.de: Guten Abend, einen Tisch für zwei, bitte.
example_sentences.en: Good evening, a table for two, please.

example_sentences.de: Einen Tisch für zwei, bitte — am liebsten draußen.
example_sentences.en: A table for two, please — outside if possible.

cloze.de: Hallo, ___ Tisch für zwei, bitte.
cloze.en: Hello, a table for two, please.

words.notes: Accusative after the implied 'Ich hätte gern': einen Tisch, not 'ein Tisch'. Swap the number: für drei, für vier.
words.mnemonic: einen = accusative masculine, because you are asking FOR a table.
words.germany_context: In many places you don't need this at all — you simply walk in and take any free table. Use it in busier or nicer restaurants.

example_sentences.de: Entschuldigung, die Speisekarte, bitte.
example_sentences.en: Excuse me, the menu, please.

example_sentences.de: Die Speisekarte, bitte, und schon mal zwei Wasser.
example_sentences.en: The menu, please, and two waters already.

cloze.de: Könnten wir bitte die ___ haben?
cloze.en: Could we have the menu, please?

words.notes: Short and perfectly polite thanks to 'bitte'. 'Die Karte, bitte' is even more common.
words.mnemonic: Any noun + bitte is a complete polite request in German.

example_sentences.de: Ich hätte gern einen Kaffee und ein Wasser.
example_sentences.en: I'd like a coffee and a water.

example_sentences.de: Ich hätte gern die Suppe als Vorspeise.
example_sentences.en: I'd like the soup as a starter.

cloze.de: Ich ___ gern ein Stück Kuchen, bitte.
cloze.en: I'd like a piece of cake, please.

words.notes: The politest way to order. What follows is accusative: einen Kaffee, ein Bier, eine Suppe.
words.mnemonic: hätte = the polite 'would have' form of haben.
words.germany_context: This is the standard, polite ordering formula everywhere — more natural than 'Ich will' and softer than 'Ich nehme'.

example_sentences.de: Ich nehme das Schnitzel mit Pommes.
example_sentences.en: I'll have the schnitzel with fries.

example_sentences.de: Und was nehmen Sie?
example_sentences.en: And what will you have?

cloze.de: Ich ___ den Salat, bitte.
cloze.en: I'll have the salad, please.

words.notes: Direct but completely normal when ordering. 'Ich hätte gern' sounds a touch more polite.
words.mnemonic: nehmen = to take, so 'I take the schnitzel'.

example_sentences.de: Zusammen oder getrennt? — Getrennt, bitte.
example_sentences.en: Together or separately? — Separately, please.

example_sentences.de: Die Kellnerin fragt immer: Zusammen oder getrennt?
example_sentences.en: The waitress always asks: together or separately?

cloze.de: Zahlen Sie zusammen oder ___?
cloze.en: Are you paying together or separately?

words.notes: The waiter's standard question. Answer with one word: 'Zusammen' or 'Getrennt'.
words.mnemonic: getrennt = separated, like getrennte Wege.
words.germany_context: Splitting the bill is completely normal in Germany, even in large groups — servers will happily go round the table and take payment from each person one by one.

example_sentences.de: Entschuldigung, die Rechnung, bitte.
example_sentences.en: Excuse me, the bill, please.

example_sentences.de: Die Rechnung, bitte, wir müssen los.
example_sentences.en: The bill, please, we have to go.

cloze.de: Könnten wir bitte die ___ haben?
cloze.en: Could we have the bill, please?

words.notes: 'Zahlen, bitte' means exactly the same and is even shorter.
words.mnemonic: Noun + bitte = polite request.
words.germany_context: Never take the bill to a counter: ask for it at your table, and the server brings the card reader or takes cash right there.

example_sentences.de: Zahlen, bitte!
example_sentences.en: The bill, please!

example_sentences.de: Er hebt die Hand und sagt: Zahlen, bitte!
example_sentences.en: He raises his hand and says: the bill, please!

cloze.de: ___, bitte! Wir möchten gehen.
cloze.en: The bill, please! We'd like to go.

words.notes: The shortest, most idiomatic way to ask to pay. Politer version: 'Ich würde gern zahlen.'
words.mnemonic: Literally 'to pay, please'.
words.germany_context: Say it while making eye contact with your server; you pay at the table, and the server will ask 'Zusammen oder getrennt?'

example_sentences.de: Hier sind 20 Euro — stimmt so.
example_sentences.en: Here's 20 euros — keep the change.

example_sentences.de: Stimmt so, vielen Dank!
example_sentences.en: Keep the change, thank you very much!

cloze.de: Das macht 18,40. — Nehmen Sie 20, ___ so.
cloze.en: That comes to 18.40. — Take 20, keep the change.

words.notes: Literally 'it's correct like that'. Only say it if you really mean the server should keep the rest.
words.mnemonic: stimmen = to be correct; so = like that.
words.germany_context: The normal tipping move: hand over a note and either say the total you want to pay ('Machen Sie 20') or simply 'Stimmt so' — roughly 5-10% rounded up.

example_sentences.de: Hat es geschmeckt? — Ja, sehr gut, danke!
example_sentences.en: Did you enjoy it? — Yes, very good, thank you!

example_sentences.de: Der Kellner fragt: Hat es Ihnen geschmeckt?
example_sentences.en: The waiter asks: did you enjoy it?

cloze.de: Hat es Ihnen ___?
cloze.en: Did you enjoy it?

words.notes: Answer simply: 'Ja, sehr gut, danke.' or 'Es war lecker.'
words.mnemonic: schmecken = to taste; the Perfekt is 'hat geschmeckt'.
words.germany_context: Servers ask this when clearing plates; a short positive answer is expected, and complaints are rare unless something was really wrong.

example_sentences.de: Guten Appetit! — Danke, gleichfalls!
example_sentences.en: Enjoy your meal! — Thanks, you too!

example_sentences.de: Der Kellner stellt den Teller hin und sagt: Guten Appetit!
example_sentences.en: The waiter puts down the plate and says: enjoy your meal!

cloze.de: Guten ___! Lass es dir schmecken.
cloze.en: Enjoy your meal! Hope you like it.

words.notes: Reply with 'Danke, gleichfalls!' if the other person is also eating.
words.mnemonic: Appetit ~ 'appetite'.
words.germany_context: Germans say it before every meal, including to colleagues in the office kitchen — not saying it feels slightly cold.

example_sentences.de: Prost! Auf deinen neuen Job!
example_sentences.en: Cheers! To your new job!

example_sentences.de: Alle heben die Gläser und rufen: Prost!
example_sentences.en: Everyone raises their glasses and shouts: cheers!

cloze.de: ___! Schön, dass ihr da seid.
cloze.en: Cheers! Great that you're here.

words.notes: 'Zum Wohl!' is the slightly more formal version, used more with wine.
words.mnemonic: From Latin 'prosit' — may it be good for you.
words.germany_context: Clink glasses with everyone individually and make eye contact each time — skipping the eye contact is a well-known superstition and looks rude.

example_sentences.de: Noch ein Bier, bitte!
example_sentences.en: Another beer, please!

example_sentences.de: Noch ein Bier, bitte, und für sie einen Wein.
example_sentences.en: Another beer, please, and a wine for her.

cloze.de: ___ ein Bier, bitte — das gleiche wie vorhin.
cloze.en: Another beer, please — the same as before.

words.notes: 'Noch ein …' = one more of the same. Swap the noun: noch einen Kaffee, noch eine Cola.
words.mnemonic: noch = still/more, so 'still one beer'.
words.germany_context: In a Kneipe the server often just nods at your empty glass and brings the next one — say 'Nein danke, wir zahlen' when you're done.

example_sentences.de: Entschuldigung, ist hier noch frei?
example_sentences.en: Excuse me, is this seat free?

example_sentences.de: Ist hier noch frei? — Ja, bitte, setzen Sie sich.
example_sentences.en: Is this seat free? — Yes, please, take a seat.

cloze.de: Ist dieser Platz noch ___?
cloze.en: Is this seat still free?

words.notes: 'Frei' here means unoccupied. The answer 'Besetzt' means it's taken.
words.mnemonic: frei = free, besetzt = occupied — the same words as on toilet doors.
words.germany_context: In a full Biergarten or café, asking this and sharing a table with strangers is completely normal and expected.

example_sentences.de: Einen Kaffee zum Mitnehmen, bitte.
example_sentences.en: A coffee to take away, please.

example_sentences.de: Zum Mitnehmen oder zum Hieressen?
example_sentences.en: To take away or to eat in?

cloze.de: Ich hätte gern eine Pizza ___ Mitnehmen.
cloze.en: I'd like a pizza to take away.

words.notes: The opposite is 'zum Hieressen' (to eat in). 'Coffee to go' is also widely understood.
words.mnemonic: mitnehmen = to take with you.
words.germany_context: Takeaway food is taxed lower than eating in, so the same dish is often a bit cheaper 'zum Mitnehmen'.

example_sentences.de: Das Lokal ist klein, aber sehr gemütlich.
example_sentences.en: The restaurant is small but very cosy.

example_sentences.de: Kennst du ein gutes Lokal in der Nähe?
example_sentences.en: Do you know a good restaurant nearby?

cloze.de: Wir haben gestern in einem griechischen ___ gegessen.
cloze.en: Yesterday we ate at a Greek restaurant.

words.notes: 'Lokal' is the everyday word for any eating and drinking place — restaurant, pub or bar.
words.mnemonic: Your local place to eat: das Lokal.

example_sentences.de: Bitte bestellen Sie an der Theke.
example_sentences.en: Please order at the counter.

example_sentences.de: An der Theke ist noch ein Platz frei.
example_sentences.en: There's still a seat free at the counter.

cloze.de: Der Kuchen liegt vorne in der ___.
cloze.en: The cake is in the counter display at the front.

words.notes: Theke = the counter in a bakery, café or pub. In a shop it's often 'die Frischetheke'.
words.mnemonic: Theke sounds a bit like 'take' — where you take your order.
words.germany_context: In bakeries and self-service cafés you order and pay at the Theke and carry the tray yourself; no tip is expected, though a coin in the Trinkgeld jar is nice.

example_sentences.de: Der Stammtisch ist immer reserviert.
example_sentences.en: The regulars' table is always reserved.

example_sentences.de: Jeden Donnerstag gibt es hier einen Stammtisch.
example_sentences.en: There's a regulars' get-together here every Thursday.

cloze.de: Setz dich nicht an den ___, der ist für die Stammgäste.
cloze.en: Don't sit at the regulars' table, it's for the regular customers.

words.notes: der Tisch → der Stammtisch. It means both the table and the group that meets there.
words.mnemonic: Stamm = trunk/core, so the table of the core crowd.
words.germany_context: A table marked 'Stammtisch' belongs to the regulars — never sit there, even in an empty pub. Joining an expat or hobby Stammtisch is a classic way to meet people.

example_sentences.de: Der Koch macht heute die Spezialität des Hauses.
example_sentences.en: The chef is making the speciality of the house today.

example_sentences.de: Mein Bruder arbeitet als Koch in einem Hotel.
example_sentences.en: My brother works as a cook in a hotel.

cloze.de: Bitte sagen Sie dem ___, dass es super geschmeckt hat.
cloze.en: Please tell the chef that it tasted great.

words.notes: Female form: die Köchin. Plural has an umlaut: die Köche.
words.mnemonic: kochen → der Koch.

example_sentences.de: Was ist heute das Tagesgericht?
example_sentences.en: What is the dish of the day today?

example_sentences.de: Das Tagesgericht kostet zehn Euro mit Suppe.
example_sentences.en: The dish of the day costs ten euros with soup.

cloze.de: Ich nehme das ___, das geht am schnellsten.
cloze.en: I'll take the dish of the day, that's the quickest.

words.notes: das Gericht → das Tagesgericht. Usually written on a board outside.
words.mnemonic: Tag + Gericht: the dish for today.
words.germany_context: The Tagesgericht is the cheapest and fastest lunch option and is often only advertised on a chalkboard by the door, not in the printed menu.

example_sentences.de: Der Mittagstisch kostet nur neun Euro.
example_sentences.en: The lunch special costs only nine euros.

example_sentences.de: Wir haben von Montag bis Freitag einen Mittagstisch.
example_sentences.en: We have a lunch special from Monday to Friday.

cloze.de: Gibt es heute einen ___?
cloze.en: Is there a lunch special today?

words.notes: der Tisch → der Mittagstisch. Usually a small daily menu at a fixed low price.
words.mnemonic: Mittag + Tisch: the midday table.
words.germany_context: Between roughly 11:30 and 14:00 many restaurants offer a Mittagstisch far cheaper than their evening menu — the standard weekday lunch for German office workers.

example_sentences.de: In der Mensa ist das Essen sehr günstig.
example_sentences.en: The food in the canteen is very cheap.

example_sentences.de: Wir treffen uns um zwölf in der Mensa.
example_sentences.en: We're meeting at twelve in the canteen.

cloze.de: Studenten essen mittags meistens in der ___.
cloze.en: Students usually eat in the canteen at lunchtime.

words.notes: 'Mensa' is the university canteen; a company one is 'die Kantine'.
words.mnemonic: Latin mensa = table.
words.germany_context: University Mensen and company Kantinen are card-only and subsidised — a hot meal often costs 4-7 euros, and guests usually pay a slightly higher price.

example_sentences.de: Hafermilch gibt es nur gegen Aufpreis.
example_sentences.en: Oat milk is only available for an extra charge.

example_sentences.de: Der Aufpreis für die Beilage beträgt zwei Euro.
example_sentences.en: The surcharge for the side dish is two euros.

cloze.de: Kostet die große Portion einen ___?
cloze.en: Does the large portion cost an extra charge?

words.notes: 'Gegen Aufpreis' = for an extra charge. You'll see it in the small print of menus.
words.mnemonic: auf + Preis: a price on top.
words.germany_context: Extras that are free elsewhere often cost here: sauces, a second slice of bread and plant milk usually carry an Aufpreis of 30 cents to a euro.

example_sentences.de: Sie haben mir zu wenig Wechselgeld gegeben.
example_sentences.en: You gave me too little change.

example_sentences.de: Der Kellner bringt gleich das Wechselgeld.
example_sentences.en: The waiter is bringing the change right away.

cloze.de: Behalten Sie das ___ als Trinkgeld.
cloze.en: Keep the change as a tip.

words.notes: das Geld → das Wechselgeld. 'Das Kleingeld' means coins in general.
words.mnemonic: wechseln = to change, so Wechselgeld = the money you get back.
words.germany_context: In cash-only places, don't hand over a 50 for a 6-euro meal — small shops and Imbisse often have very little Wechselgeld.

example_sentences.de: Einmal Currywurst mit Pommes, bitte.
example_sentences.en: One currywurst with fries, please.

example_sentences.de: Zweimal Schnitzel und einmal Salat, bitte.
example_sentences.en: Two schnitzels and one salad, please.

cloze.de: ___ das Tagesgericht, bitte.
cloze.en: One of the dish of the day, please.

words.notes: Very idiomatic for ordering food: einmal, zweimal, dreimal + the dish. No article needed.
words.mnemonic: ein + mal = one time, i.e. one portion.
words.germany_context: This is how people order at an Imbiss or a busy counter — short, fast and completely normal.

example_sentences.de: Entschuldigung, wir möchten bestellen.
example_sentences.en: Excuse me, we'd like to order.

example_sentences.de: Wir möchten bestellen, wir haben nicht viel Zeit.
example_sentences.en: We'd like to order, we don't have much time.

cloze.de: Wir ___ bestellen, bitte.
cloze.en: We'd like to order, please.

words.notes: Use it to call the server over. Singular: 'Ich möchte bestellen.'
words.mnemonic: möchten = would like, the polite form of wollen.
words.germany_context: Servers won't hover; if nobody comes, catch their eye or say this as they pass — it isn't considered rude.

example_sentences.de: Was können Sie empfehlen? — Nehmen Sie den Braten.
example_sentences.en: What do you recommend? — Take the roast.

example_sentences.de: Wir kennen die Karte nicht. Was können Sie empfehlen?
example_sentences.en: We don't know the menu. What do you recommend?

cloze.de: Was ___ Sie empfehlen?
cloze.en: What do you recommend?

words.notes: With friends use 'du': 'Was kannst du empfehlen?'
words.mnemonic: empfehlen = to recommend.
words.germany_context: A safe move when the menu is only in German — servers will usually point at the Tageskarte or the house speciality.

example_sentences.de: Sonst noch etwas? — Nein, das war's, danke.
example_sentences.en: Anything else? — No, that's all, thanks.

example_sentences.de: Zwei Brötchen und einen Kaffee. Das war's, danke.
example_sentences.en: Two rolls and a coffee. That's all, thanks.

cloze.de: Nein danke, das ___, wir zahlen bitte.
cloze.en: No thanks, that's all, we'd like to pay please.

words.notes: 'War's' is short for 'war es'. The staff question is 'Sonst noch etwas?'
words.mnemonic: Literally 'that was it'.
words.germany_context: You'll hear 'Sonst noch etwas?' at every bakery counter — this is the standard one-line answer.

example_sentences.de: Mit Karte oder bar? — Mit Karte, bitte.
example_sentences.en: By card or cash? — By card, please.

example_sentences.de: Zahlen Sie mit Karte oder bar?
example_sentences.en: Are you paying by card or cash?

cloze.de: Ich zahle ___, ich habe genug Geld dabei.
cloze.en: I'll pay cash, I have enough money on me.

words.notes: 'Bar' as an adverb means 'in cash': bar zahlen.
words.mnemonic: bar zahlen = pay with Bargeld.
words.germany_context: Ask 'Kann man mit Karte zahlen?' before you order — plenty of Kneipen, Imbisse and small cafés are still cash-only, and many take only German Girocard.

example_sentences.de: Ich nehme den Döner. Ohne Zwiebeln, bitte.
example_sentences.en: I'll have the doner kebab. Without onions, please.

example_sentences.de: Ohne Zwiebeln, bitte, und mit extra Soße.
example_sentences.en: Without onions, please, and with extra sauce.

cloze.de: ___ Zwiebeln, bitte, die mag ich nicht.
cloze.en: Without onions, please, I don't like them.

words.notes: 'Ohne' takes the accusative. Swap the word: ohne Zwiebeln, ohne Käse, ohne Fleisch.
words.mnemonic: ohne = without; the opposite is 'mit'.
words.germany_context: Kitchens are usually happy to leave something out, but ask when ordering — changes after the food arrives are not welcome.

example_sentences.de: Entschuldigung, wo ist die Toilette?
example_sentences.en: Excuse me, where is the toilet?

example_sentences.de: Wo ist die Toilette? — Hinten links.
example_sentences.en: Where is the toilet? — At the back on the left.

cloze.de: Wo ___ die Toilette, bitte?
cloze.en: Where is the toilet, please?

words.notes: Doors are marked 'Damen' (women) and 'Herren' (men). 'WC' works everywhere too.
words.mnemonic: Toilette ~ 'toilet', feminine like most -ette words.
words.germany_context: Public toilets usually cost 50-70 cents, and even in restaurants an attendant may have a plate for coins — another reason to carry small change.

example_sentences.de: Ich vertrage kein Gluten.
example_sentences.en: I can't tolerate gluten.

example_sentences.de: Sie verträgt keine Milch, aber Käse geht.
example_sentences.en: She can't tolerate milk, but cheese is fine.

cloze.de: Ich ___ keine Laktose, haben Sie etwas anderes?
cloze.en: I can't tolerate lactose, do you have something else?

words.notes: Strong verb: du verträgst, er verträgt. Stronger version: 'Ich bin allergisch gegen …'
words.mnemonic: vertragen = to tolerate/bear something.
words.germany_context: Say it when you order; German menus mark allergens with small numbers, and staff can check the Allergenliste in the kitchen for you.
